blocks.text: Different treatment methods are used depending on the type and severity of pollution, such as organic matter, chemicals or pathogens. They are used at different levels of treatment: primary treatment (removal of physical debris), secondary treatment (biological processing) and tertiary treatment (chemical purification). The main steps are as follows.

items: Screening and sedimentation: large insoluble particles are removed by passing the water through metal screens. In sedimentation the water is held in large tanks so that suspended solids settle to the bottom under gravity.

Coagulation and flocculation: to speed up the settling of fine colloidal particles, a chemical coagulant such as aluminium sulphate, Al2(SO4)3, is added when needed; dissolved contaminants (such as heavy metals and phosphates) are also precipitated in insoluble forms. The small particles clump together into larger masses called floc, which are easily removed.

Filtration: the water then passes through layers of graded sand and gravel, a mechanical process that removes the remaining fine suspended matter and some microorganisms; the sand traps particles in the pores between its grains. Activated carbon is used for more advanced purification.

Disinfection: filtration cannot remove dissolved ions or microscopic pathogens, so chemical treatment is needed. Chlorination is the most common method; others use sodium hypochlorite (NaOCl), ozone (O3) or sometimes hydrogen peroxide (H2O2). Chlorine or sodium hypochlorite forms hypochlorous acid (HOCl) in water, which gets into bacteria and viruses and disrupts their cell functions.

Reverse osmosis (RO) and ion exchange: for high-purity water, such as for laboratories, or in very salty regions. RO uses a semi-permeable membrane that, under pressure, lets water through but holds back dissolved salts, bacteria and other impurities. Ion exchange is used to 'soften' water: hard water contains high concentrations of Ca2+ and Mg2+ ions, which interfere with industrial processes and soap, and in an ion-exchange column these ions are swapped for Na+ or H+ ions.
